```{r}
#| label: setup
library(brms)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)
library(loo)
library(priorsense)
library(tidyverse)
options(brms.backend = "cmdstanr", mc.cores = 4)
fit_dir <- here::here("output", "fits")
theme_set(bayesplot::theme_default())
```

# Introduction

Motivation, the problem, and the main modelling idea. An illustrative figure helps.

# Data

Source, how it was collected and preprocessed, and whether it has been analysed
online before (cite it and explain how this analysis differs).

```{r}
#| label: data
#| eval: false
d <- read_csv(here::here("data", "processed", "data.csv"))
```

# Models

At least two models, e.g. a non-hierarchical and a hierarchical one. Write each
model in mathematical notation.

# Priors

Proper priors for every parameter, with a justification (weakly informative or
informative). List any default priors left unchanged; note that brms uses flat
priors for regression coefficients by default.

```{r}
#| label: priors
#| eval: false
priors_m1 <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sigma")
)
```

# Model code

```{r}
#| label: fit-models
#| eval: false
m1 <- brm(y ~ x, data = d, prior = priors_m1,
          chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, seed = 2026,
          file = file.path(fit_dir, "m1"))
m2 <- brm(y ~ x + (1 | group), data = d, prior = priors_m2,
          chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, seed = 2026,
          file = file.path(fit_dir, "m2"))
```

# Inference details

Chains, iterations, warmup, and the exact sampling call used.

# Convergence diagnostics

R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, and divergences for all models. Summarise when there are
no problems, and describe any fixes.

```{r}
#| label: convergence
#| eval: false
summarise_draws(as_draws_df(m1), default_convergence_measures())
nuts_params(m1) |> filter(Parameter == "divergent__") |> summarise(sum(Value))
```

# Posterior predictive checks

Checks suited to the outcome type (density overlays for continuous data,
calibration plots for binary/ordinal, rootograms for counts).

```{r}
#| label: ppc
#| eval: false
pp_check(m1, ndraws = 100)
```

# Prior sensitivity analysis

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity
#| eval: false
powerscale_sensitivity(m1)
```

# Model comparison

PSIS-LOO with uncertainty, plus practical measures where relevant. State the
preferred model and why.

```{r}
#| label: loo
#| eval: false
loo_compare(loo(m1), loo(m2))
```
